text_blocks.snippet: Strep throat typically clears up within a week with antibiotic treatment. Symptoms like sore throat, fever, and difficulty swallowing usually begin to improve within one to two days of starting antibiotics. While some individuals may feel better in a few days, a full course of antibiotics (usually 10 days) is crucial to prevent complications and ensure the bacteria is eradicated.

text_blocks.snippet: Strep throat is a bacterial infection of the throat and tonsils, caused by group A Streptococcus bacteria. It is highly contagious and can spread through droplets from coughs or sneezes, or by touching contaminated surfaces. While most strep throat cases are not serious and can be treated with antibiotics, it's crucial to seek medical attention, especially in children, as untreated strep throat can lead to serious complications like rheumatic fever.
snippet_highlighted_words: a bacterial infection of the throat and tonsils, caused by group A Streptococcus bacteria

list.snippet: Sore throat: This is the most common symptom and can range from mild to severe.
Painful swallowing: Swallowing can be difficult and painful due to the throat inflammation.
Fever: A fever, often starting suddenly and peaking on the second day, is common.
Swollen and tender lymph nodes: The lymph nodes in the neck may be swollen and painful to the touch.
White patches or pus on the tonsils: White patches or pus may be visible on the tonsils at the back of the throat.
Red spots on the roof of the mouth: Small, red spots may appear on the roof of the mouth.
Headache and body aches: These symptoms can accompany the sore throat and fever.
Strep throat is highly contagious and can be spread easily from person to person through respiratory droplets.
The infection is usually contagious for 2-5 days after exposure, and can be contagious for up to a month if left untreated.
Antibiotics are necessary to treat strep throat and prevent complications.
It's important to see a doctor for diagnosis and treatment, especially if symptoms are severe or persistent.
If you experience severe difficulty breathing or swallowing.
If you have a high fever, purple or blood-colored spots on the skin.
If symptoms don't improve after 48 hours of antibiotic treatment.
If you experience nausea, vomiting, earache, headache, skin rash, or painful joints.
If you have any concerns about your symptoms, it's always best to consult a healthcare professional.
